clue.text: Fine tune for commercial fair

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, a short advertisement
just means fair or equitable

explanation.surface: Someone polishing up a television advert to make it fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To make fine changes to something so it works properly is a synonym for making small corrections.

clue.text: Many sick of Irish diet

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, crossword shorthand for many
to ail is to be sick or unwell

explanation.surface: Lots of people made ill by what they eat in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' looks like food but means a parliament or assembly; the Dail (Dáil Éireann) is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, and the Dail is the chamber of Ireland's national parliament.

clue.text: Nude type without dress given sack

definitions.meaning: read literally, someone with no frock on, undressed
a priest given the sack is stripped of clerical office

explanation.surface: A naked person, out of frock, has been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest who is defrocked is expelled from the clergy, dismissed from the priesthood like being sacked; literally it also suggests having no frock on.

clue.text: Tank starts with advantage, namely armour plate

indicators.note: the start of the word tank is its opening letter only

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: Tank warfare begins with an edge in armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasset is one of the overlapping metal plates of medieval armour protecting the thigh.

clue.text: Outrageous bombast with a banner

parts.note: a flag is a banner
a rant is bombastic, ranting speech

explanation.surface: A ranting demonstrator waving a banner is behaving scandalously.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant behaviour is glaring and shocking, a synonym for outrageous.

clue.text: Last word in remote Surrey residence

parts.note: far means distant or remote
Ewell is a town in Surrey, the county south-west of London
your address is where you reside

explanation.surface: Final remarks made at an out-of-the-way house in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: EWELL is a town in Surrey, an English county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A valedictory speech given on leaving is a parting statement, so a speaker's last word.

clue.text: Complaints of terminal's outright chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
read as out right: the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: the word terminal's, the possessive giving its S

explanation.surface: Grumbles about total disorder at an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outright' splits as 'out R(ight)': R leaves TERMINALS to give TEMINALS, and 'chaos' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are illnesses or disorders, the same as maladies.

clue.text: Prepare for conflict that's a back number

parts.note: the rear is the back
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: An old magazine issue tells you how to get ready for war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back number' looks like an old issue of a periodical, but splits into REAR (back) and M (a number).
explanation.definitionFit: To equip again with weapons is to make ready for fighting.

clue.text: Sensible ban on Lear, perhaps

parts.note: no as a refusal or prohibition
Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse, so his work exemplifies it

explanation.surface: A ban on King Lear might seem reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' tempts toward Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear, the Victorian writer of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-nonsense person is practical and down-to-earth, hence sensible.

clue.text: Disagree about American broadcaster

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to differ is to disagree

explanation.surface: Arguing over an American radio presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A diffuser spreads something widely, as a broadcaster scatters something abroad.

clue.text: Found out about service channel

indicators.note: the channel is wrapped about the service, containing it

parts.note: a leat is an open channel carrying water to a mill
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Discovering facts about a military communications channel.
explanation.walkthrough: A LEAT is a watercourse feeding a mill wheel; the RN is Britain's Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have found out a fact is to have learned or discovered it.

clue.text: Right wheel moving erratically is unstoppable

indicators.note: moving erratically means irregularly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runaway wheel, swerving to the right, cannot be halted.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming force is irresistible, too strong to resist or halt.

clue.text: Hearsay over footer scrimmage before this

parts.note: hear say: the word hear, said aloud, gives the word meaning in this place

indicators.note: a scrimmage is a confused scuffle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rumours about a football scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearsay' looks like rumour but splits as 'hear' plus 'say', the word spoken; 'footer' is old British slang for football, and 'over' sets the first piece above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretofore is a formal word meaning until now or previously, i.e. prior to this time.

clue.text: Scots' retreat from stated strike

indicators.note: stated signals a word spoken aloud

parts.note: to nuke is to strike with nuclear weapons

explanation.surface: A Scottish withdrawal after a declared attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuk is the Scots form of nook, a sheltered corner or hideaway.

clue.text: Heads of the fleet?

parts.note: looks like the admirals in command, but heads are a sailor's word for ship toilets

explanation.surface: A question about who commands the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the toilets are called the heads, and military toilets are also called by this name.

clue.text: Make a charge from analysis of paint clue

indicators.note: an analysis breaks the words down, so their letters are taken apart and remade

explanation.surface: Forensic study of a paint sample leads to an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculpate someone is to accuse or incriminate them, bringing a charge.

clue.text: Soaks reported in pancreatic enzyme

indicators.note: reported signals that the word is said aloud

parts.note: steeps means soaks

explanation.surface: Drinkers mentioned in a medical text about digestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaks' looks like heavy drinkers but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Steapsin is the lipase secreted by the pancreas, an enzyme that digests fats.

clue.text: To sell Tate works means lasting strife

parts.note: to vend is to sell

indicators.note: works as in reworks: the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to sell off the Tate's artworks causes long-running bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like paintings at the Tate gallery, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud, a bitter quarrel that persists.

clue.text: Suit and its holder

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit is a legal action
a container for a suit of clothes, as in a suitcase

explanation.definitionFit: A legal case is a suit brought in court, and a case is also a container that holds clothes.

clue.text: Mechanic less liable to 6

definitions.meaning: a person who assembles or repairs machinery
healthier, less prone to complaints and illnesses

explanation.definitionFit: A fitter is a mechanic who assembles parts; as a comparative it means healthier, less prone to illness.

clue.text: Left light on — what's thereby increased on the south coast?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to light on something is to land on it
leaving the lights on increases the electricity bill

explanation.surface: Leaving a lamp on just pushes up the energy costs.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTLAND BILL is a headland at the tip of the Isle of Portland in Dorset, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This headland in Dorset is a landmark on England's southern coastline.

clue.text: Traditional tax collector is possessive

parts.note: the definite article, as in the familiar 'the taxman'
IR is the Inland Revenue, the old British tax authority

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned taxman is grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue (IR) was Britain's tax-collecting body until 2005, traditionally called 'the IR'.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a possessive determiner, showing that something belongs to them.

clue.text: This sounds like a dominant idea

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be said aloud

parts.note: this very thing you are reading is a crossword clue

explanation.surface: A remark that seems to be a central concept.
explanation.definitionFit: A clou is the chief point of interest or central idea, from French for nail.

clue.text: In sport, English show their guts

indicators.note: the English letter goes in the sport

parts.note: bowls is a sport played on a green

explanation.surface: English players display their courage at the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestines are the guts, the internal organs of digestion.

clue.text: 23 despatched by train, start to finish

indicators.note: the first letter is moved from the start to the end

parts.note: sent means despatched
goods go by rail

explanation.surface: Something sent by rail, from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTRAIL with its first letter moved to the end becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are intestines, the same internal organs as guts.

clue.text: Wheels depend on them for knowing which way to go

definitions.meaning: ball or roller parts that let wheels turn freely
one's sense of position and direction

explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings let wheels spin, and finding one's position means getting your sense of direction.

clue.text: Primate may be positive or negative

definitions.meaning: a macaque monkey of South Asia
the blood factor named after that monkey, present or absent in blood

explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, and the Rh blood factor named after it is positive or negative.
